chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Sahl al-Qurshi who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the meat of the dog. He said: 'It is a morphed creature (mash).' I said: 'It is haram (forbidden)?' He said: 'It is najis (impure).' I repeated the question to him three times, and each time he said: 'It is najis.'

key_terms.حَرَامٌ: Haram: forbidden, prohibited by Islamic law
key_terms.مَسْخٌ: Mash: divine metamorphosis or transformation as divine punishment, the belief that certain animals originated from transformed humans
key_terms.نَجَسٌ: Najis: ritually impure, a legal category in Islamic jurisprudence indicating a substance that makes other things impure on contact

ai.seo_question: Is dog meat haram or najis in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Abu Sahl al-Qurshi asks Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) about the status of dog meat. The Imam's response is notable: rather than simply declaring it 'haram', he emphasizes that it is 'najis' (ritually impure), a stronger classification. The concept of 'mash' (divine metamorphosis) refers to the belief that dogs were among creatures that resulted from divine punishment transforming humans or other creatures, making them inherently impure.
